requirement:
Colon-fenced directives and fenced code blocks have anonymous `block` nodes
with selectors under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
A block contains its opening fence, body, and closing fence when present.
Its parent is the nearest enclosing outline container.
An unclosed colon fence retains its block through the end of the enclosing
file or directive body, excluding the enclosing directive's closing fence.
rationale:
I judged the tests adequate for `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fenced_blocks`. I did not request implementation source. The supplied tests in `crates/habeas-sdk/src/outline/markdown_tests.rs` cover each obligation.

**1. Anonymous `block` nodes with `block@hash` selectors.**
- `paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges` covers a nested colon directive and a closed backtick code block. For every non-section node it asserts that the segment starts with `block@` and has the expected hash length. It also asserts that `outline.resolve(&node.selector)` returns the node's index.
- `unfinished_code_fences_remain_literal_blocks_through_eof` asserts the same segment shape for unclosed backtick and tilde code fences.
- `literal_code_inline_code_and_html_shield_directive_looking_text` checks the cases that must not produce blocks:
  - A longer backtick fence or a tilde fence containing `:::{note}` yields exactly one block and no paragraph.
  - A ```` ```{note} ```` fence yields one block.
  - Inline code, HTML, and comment text yield no block.

**2. A block holds its opening fence, body and closing fence when present.**
- The first test compares `node_lines` with the source byte slice for each node, and it checks the exact line ranges of the blocks.
- `nested_fence_lengths_and_closer_whitespace_preserve_the_right_containers` checks line ranges for nested colon blocks of different lengths. A closer followed by trailing text is not treated as a closer. A closer followed by trailing whitespace is. A closed tilde code block holds `::::::` and `:::{fake}` literally.
- `empty_long_closed_and_quoted_directives_keep_original_unicode_offsets` covers an empty directive, a closer longer than the opener, and a quoted CRLF Unicode directive with line ranges.

**3. Parent is the nearest enclosing outline container.**
- The first test checks the parents of the blocks and paragraphs: a block under a section, a block under a block, and a paragraph under a block.
- The nested-fence test checks that both the inner directive and the code block have the outer block as parent.
- The unclosed-fence tests check that the parent is the section, using `section[H]` and `section[Outside]`.

**4. An unclosed colon fence runs through the end of the enclosing file or directive body, excluding the enclosing closer.**
- `unfinished_directives_retain_their_body_and_leave_the_outer_closer_outside` covers four file-level unclosed cases: with and without a trailing newline, with a heading inside the body, and after a preceding heading. Each asserts that the block ends at the end of the source and has the section parent.
- The same test covers an unclosed inner `:::{tip}` inside an outer `::::::{note}`. The inner block ends before the outer closer, and its text does not contain the outer closer. The outer block spans its full range, and the inner block's parent is the outer block. Trailing prose after the outer block belongs to the section.

The tests contain real assertions for each case. All are marked `{test}` for the subject.

I found no obligation or named boundary case without a test.

text: Colon-fenced directives and fenced code blocks have anonymous `block` nodes
A block contains its opening fence, body, and closing fence when present.
Its parent is the nearest enclosing outline container.
An unclosed colon fence retains its block through the end of the enclosing
file or directive body, excluding the enclosing directive's closing fence.
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
